headline: Azure and AI strength fuel broad growth, margins expand
summary_short: Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 revenue rose 18% y/y to $90.0 billion on continued Azure and AI cloud strength, with GAAP diluted EPS up 32% y/y to $4.81, including a $3.2 billion gain from its Anthropic investment.
summary_long: Fiscal Q4 revenue grew 18% y/y (17% constant currency) to $90.0B, led by Microsoft Cloud revenue of $59.3B (+27%) and Azure (+43%); Intelligent Cloud grew 32%, Productivity and Business Processes grew 14%, while More Personal Computing fell 4% on weaker Windows OEM and Xbox content revenue. Operating income rose 18% to $40.6B; net income rose 31% to $35.8B and diluted EPS rose 32% to $4.81, boosted $0.27/share by a $3.2B Anthropic gain and lower Voluntary Retirement Program costs, partly offset by Xbox severance and impairment charges. Non-GAAP EPS (ex-OpenAI effects) was $4.74, +23%. Cash and short-term investments fell to $76.8B from $94.6B y/y; Microsoft returned $10.2B to shareholders via dividends and buybacks.

drivers.explanation: CEO Nadella cited Azure revenue surpassing $100B for the year and Microsoft 365 Copilot reaching over 30 million paid seats as signs of AI momentum; CFO Hood highlighted $59.3B Microsoft Cloud revenue, up 27% y/y.

Growth driven by Microsoft Cloud revenue of $59.3B (+27%) and Azure (+43%), plus double-digit gains across Microsoft 365, LinkedIn and Dynamics 365, partly offset by a 4% decline in More Personal Computing on weaker Windows OEM and Xbox revenue.
Diluted EPS was boosted $0.27/share versus April guidance by a $3.2B Anthropic investment gain and lower Voluntary Retirement Program costs, partly offset by Xbox severance and impairment charges.
Net income growth reflects the same discrete items as EPS: a $3.2B Anthropic gain and lower Voluntary Retirement Program costs, partly offset by Xbox severance and impairment charges.
Cash and short-term investments fell as $54.8B used in investing (mostly $35.8B of capex) and $11.8B used in financing outweighed $55.4B of operating cash flow this quarter.
